newsitem.title: USA: Calif. says state revenues below February forecast.
newsitem.headline: Calif. says state revenues below February forecast.

text.p: California general fund revenues for February were $21 million below the governor's 1997/98 budget forecast of $3.214 billion, the state's Department of Finance said on Tuesday.
Despite February's results, the department said year-to-date revenues were $277 million, or 0.9 percent, above the budget forecast.

Personal income tax receipts were $25 million above the month's forecast, while withholding revenues were $71 million below the governor's budget estimate, the department said in its monthly budget report.

Sales and use-tax revenues were $71 million below the month's estimate largely because of cash flow factors, the department said. Bank and corporation tax revenues were $15 million below the month's estimate because of higher-than-expected refunds, the department said.
Revenues from the insurance, estate, alcoholic beverage, tobacco and horse-racing taxes were $7 million above the month's forecast, the department said.
